name: Transport in animals and human circulatory system

questions.q: What type of circulatory system do humans and other vertebrates possess?
a: An open circulatory system with hemolymph

questions.q: What is the primary advantage of a double circulatory system compared to a single circulatory system?
a: It allows blood to flow slower through organs
Blood can be pumped at higher pressures, maintaining efficient oxygen delivery to body tissues after passing through the lungs
It requires only a single-chambered heart
It mixes oxygenated and deoxygenated blood completely

questions.q: Which chamber of the human heart pumps deoxygenated blood toward the lungs via the pulmonary artery?
Which blood vessel returns oxygenated blood from the lungs back to the left atrium of the heart?
What is the main structural feature that distinguishes arteries from veins?
a: Arteries have thick, elastic, muscular walls to withstand high pressure; veins have thinner walls with valves to prevent backflow
Arteries contain pocket valves; veins do not
Veins have thicker muscle layers than arteries

questions.q: What is the function of capillaries in the circulatory system?
a: To pump blood across long distances
To allow the rapid exchange of materials (such as oxygen, glucose, and carbon dioxide) between blood and body tissues through extremely thin walls

questions.q: What prevents the backflow of blood from the ventricles back into the atria when the ventricles contract?
What is the role of the coronary arteries supplying the heart muscle?
a: To pump blood into the lungs
To drain deoxygenated blood into the right atrium
To carry oxygenated blood and nutrients directly to the heart muscle cells (myocardium)

questions.q: Which component of blood is primarily responsible for transporting oxygen combined with hemoglobin?
What is the main function of white blood cells in the human body?
a: Defending the body against pathogens through phagocytosis and antibody production

questions.q: What role do blood platelets play in the circulatory system?
a: Releasing chemical factors that trigger blood clotting to seal wounds and prevent pathogen entry

questions.q: What is the straw-colored liquid component of blood that transports dissolved nutrients, hormones, urea, and carbon dioxide?
Which blood vessel carries oxygenated blood away from the left ventricle to the rest of the body?
What is the function of semi-lunar valves located at the base of the aorta and pulmonary artery?
a: To stop blood from entering the atria
To prevent the backflow of blood from the arteries back into the ventricles after ventricular contraction
To separate oxygenated and deoxygenated blood

questions.q: What causes the characteristic 'lub-dub' sound of a beating heart?
a: The closing of the heart valves (atrioventricular valves followed by semi-lunar valves)

questions.q: Why does the left ventricle have a much thicker muscular wall than the right ventricle?
a: Because it only pumps blood to the lungs
Because it does not use oxygen
Because it receives blood directly from the lungs
Because it must generate higher pressure to pump blood all the way around the entire systemic circulation (body), whereas the right ventricle pumps only to nearby lungs

questions.q: What condition occurs when fatty plaques (atheroma) build up inside the coronary arteries, potentially leading to a myocardial infarction (heart attack)?
Which lifestyle factor significantly increases the risk of developing coronary heart disease and hypertension?
a: Smoking tobacco, consuming high saturated fats, and lack of exercise

questions.q: How is tissue fluid formed from capillaries?
a: By active transport of water from cells
By red blood cells squeezing through walls
By blood plasma leaking out through the gaps in capillary walls under high hydrostatic pressure, bathing surrounding cells
By lymph vessels pumping fluid backward

questions.q: What happens to excess tissue fluid that does not reabsorb directly back into capillary blood ends?
a: It forms urine in the kidneys
It enters the lymphatic system as lymph and is eventually returned to the bloodstream

questions.q: Which of the following blood vessels contains valves and carries deoxygenated blood back toward the heart from the lower body?
What is the role of the pacemaker (sinotrial node) in the heart?
a: To generate electrical impulses that spread across the atria, initiating regular contractions of the heart muscle
To filter urea from blood plasma

questions.q: Why do capillary walls consist of a single layer of flattened squamous cells (one cell thick)?
a: To withstand very high blood pressure
To provide a short diffusion distance, maximizing the exchange rate of substances between blood and tissues
To prevent white blood cells from escaping

questions.q: What is the main function of lymph nodes found along the lymphatic system network?
a: Filtering lymph fluid and harboring lymphocytes to destroy trapped pathogens and bacteria

questions.q: Which of the following vessels transports deoxygenated blood from the body tissues into the right atrium?
How do heart valves ensure unidirectional blood flow?
a: By opening when blood pushes forward and snapping shut to prevent backflow when pressure reverses

questions.q: What is the primary effect of adrenaline hormone on the cardiovascular system during periods of fear or vigorous exercise?
a: It slows down the heart rate and constricts airways
It stops blood flow to muscles
It increases heart rate and stroke volume, directing more blood to skeletal muscles for respiration

questions.q: Which of the following correctly describes a feature of red blood cells?
a: They contain a large prominent nucleus
They are shaped like long fibers
They are biconcave discs lacking a nucleus, packed with hemoglobin to maximize oxygen transport

questions.q: What is the medical term for high blood pressure, which places excessive strain on arteries and the heart?
Which of the following lifestyle changes can help reduce the risk of cardiovascular disease?
a: Adopting a balanced diet low in saturated fats, stopping smoking, and engaging in regular aerobic exercise
Eliminating all water from the diet

questions.q: What is the role of the septum in the human heart?
a: To pump blood into the aorta
To physically separate the left side (oxygenated blood) from the right side (deoxygenated blood)

questions.q: Which type of blood vessel has the slowest blood flow velocity, facilitating maximum time for nutrient and gas exchange with tissues?
What process describes white blood cells changing shape to engulf and digest invading bacteria?
Which of the following blood components is a cellular fragment produced in bone marrow that aids in clotting?
Why is the pulmonary circulation separate from the systemic circulation in mammals?
a: To allow blood to bypass the heart entirely
To ensure blood is oxygenated in the lungs under low pressure before being pumped at high pressure through the systemic circulation to the body
To mix oxygenated and deoxygenated blood for efficiency

questions.q: Which of the following describes the pathway of blood flow through the human heart starting from the body?
a: Left atrium -> Left ventricle -> Lungs -> Right atrium
Lungs -> Pulmonary vein -> Right atrium -> Aorta
Vena cava -> Right atrium -> Right ventricle -> Pulmonary artery -> Lungs

questions.q: What happens to heart rate during physical exercise?
a: It increases to supply working muscles with more oxygen and glucose for increased aerobic respiration while removing carbon dioxide faster
It remains completely constant regardless of exertion

questions.q: Which of the following substances is transported dissolved in blood plasma?
a: Carbon dioxide (as bicarbonate ions), dissolved nutrients (glucose, amino acids), hormones, and urea

questions.q: What is the function of the bicuspid (mitral) valve in the heart?
a: To prevent backflow between the right atrium and right ventricle
To prevent backflow from the aorta
To prevent backflow of blood from the left ventricle into the left atrium during ventricular contraction
To stop blood entering pulmonary veins

questions.q: Which blood vessel delivers oxygenated blood from the aorta to the kidney tissues?
